FunctionsAdapter:
/**
 * Functions backend adapter
 * Works with any collection dynamically (collection name passed per operation)
 * Assumes Functions are named: `get_${collection}`, `create_${collection}`, etc.
 *
 * All backends go through ICallableProvider. If none configured, falls back to FirebaseCallableProvider.
 *
 * @version 0.1.0
 * @since 0.0.1
 * @author AMBROISE PARK Consulting
 */
export declare class FunctionsAdapter implements ICrudAdapter {
    readonly serverSideOnly = true;
    /**
     * Resolve ICallableProvider from provider registry.
     * Consumer must configure via configureProviders({ callable: adapter }).
     */
    private getCallable;
    /**
     * Get callable function invoker. Always uses ICallableProvider (configured or Firebase fallback).
     */
    private getCallableFn;
    get<T>(collectionName: string, id: string, schema: dndevSchema<unknown>): Promise<T | null>;
    set<T>(collectionName: string, id: string, data: T, schema: dndevSchema<T>): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>;
    update<T>(collectionName: string, id: string, data: Partial<T>): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>;
    delete(collectionName: string, id: string): Promise<void>;
    /**
     * Bulk transactional operation via the `bulk_${collection}` callable.
     *
     * @description Delegates atomicity, per-op ACL, and row validation to the
     *   server-side `bulk_${collection}` callable registered by
     *   `createCrudFunctions`. This client adapter is a thin pass-through:
     *
     *   1. `detectBulkCollisions(ops)` — rejects ambiguous payloads (same id in
     *      two buckets) before any network call. The thrown
     *      {@link BulkCollisionError} is not wrapped so callers can `instanceof`
     *      it.
     *   2. Empty bulk is a no-op — if all three arrays are empty/absent we return
     *      a zeroed {@link BulkResult} without issuing a callable. Matches the
     *      server's empty-bulk contract and avoids a needless round-trip.
     *   3. Validates the wire body with {@link BulkRequestSchema} before sending
     *      — malformed payloads fail loud locally.
     *   4. Invokes the callable via the provider registry (identical path to
     *      `add` / `update` / `delete`).
     *   5. Validates the server reply with {@link validateBulkOutcome} — a
     *      malformed server response surfaces as a clean error, never as a
     *      silent zeroed result.
     *   6. Any other failure is wrapped via {@link wrapCrudError} to preserve
     *      parity with sibling methods on this adapter.
     *
     * @param collection - Target collection (drives the callable name).
     * @param ops - Bulk operations to perform. All buckets are optional.
     * @param _schema - Intentionally unused — the server re-validates each
     *   insert against the authoritative `createSchema` bound to the entity.
     *   Matches how `add()` delegates validation server-side.
     * @param _options - Intentionally unused at the adapter layer. Per-op audit
     *   and rate-limit live in the service layer.
     * @returns The server-echoed ids, order-preserved per bucket.
     *
     * @throws {BulkCollisionError} Propagated unwrapped when the payload carries
     *   the same id in two mutually-exclusive buckets.
     * @throws {DoNotDevError} Wrapped via {@link wrapCrudError} for any
     *   callable-side failure or malformed server response.
     *
     * @example
     * ```typescript
     * const adapter = new FunctionsAdapter();
     * const result = await adapter.bulk<Event>('events', {
     *   inserts: [{ title: 'A' }, { title: 'B' }],
     *   updates: [{ id: 'e1', patch: { title: 'renamed' } }],
     *   deletes: ['e2'],
     * });
     * // result.insertedIds: ['evt_…', 'evt_…']
     * // result.updatedIds:  ['e1']
     * // result.deletedIds:  ['e2']
     * ```
     */
    bulk<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(collection: string, ops: BulkOperations<T>, _schema?: dndevSchema<T>, _options?: CrudOperationOptions): Promise<BulkResult>;
    add<T>(collectionName: string, data: T, schema?: dndevSchema<T>): Promise<{
        id: string;
        data: Record<string, unknown>;
    }>;
    query<T>(collectionName: string, options: FunctionsQueryOptions, schema: dndevSchema<unknown>, schemaType?: ListSchemaType): Promise<PaginatedQueryResult<T>>;
    subscribe<T>(): () => void;
    subscribeToCollection<T>(): () => void;
}

useEntityForm:
/**
 * Creates a type-safe form instance from an entity definition.
 *
 * Automatically binds translations to `[entity.namespace, 'crud']`, including
 * language changes and the SSR request language. No `t` option is needed for
 * normal framework usage; each entity form resolves its own namespace.
 * Pass `options.t` only to override the default namespace resolution with your
 * own translator. It replaces the default translator, rather than extending it.
 * Pass the returned `form.t` to every FormFieldRenderer / DisplayFieldRenderer,
 * including nested field-array fields. Do not duplicate entity labels in page locales.
 * The viewer role is not inferred: pass the actual `viewerRole` (default: guest).
 * Prefer EntityFormRenderer from @donotdev/ui when no custom layout is needed.
 *
 * Simple, predictable behavior:
 * - Edit mode: defaultValues (DB object) is accepted as-is and becomes `form.record`
 *   and the form's initial values from the first render (server render included);
 *   auto-save to FormStore
 * - Create mode: schema/caller defaults, auto-save to FormStore
 * - Draft restored on mount with dismissible toast (with the `form.record` it was
 *   saved with, so a concurrency token read from it stays the draft's base version)
 * - Validation `mode` default `'onTouched'`: a field's first error shows when the user
 *   leaves it, then it re-validates on every change (the fix clears it while typing).
 *   A field whose `conditions` make it required (or optional) is re-validated at that
 *   change only once touched, edited, in error, or after a submit: never flagged before.
 *   An invalid submit focuses the first invalid control (DOM order), scrolls it into
 *   view and toasts the fields to fix.
 *
 * Form state, local draft and payload hold only the fields the form writes
 * (entity descriptor, design 3.4): inputs editable for the viewer and operation,
 * `editable: 'computed'` fields (shown read-only, written), their i18n companions,
 * and `id` on edit. Generated, technical, `editable: false` and role-denied fields
 * never enter them: read them from `form.record`. `handleSubmit(onValid)` passes
 * `onValid` the resolver's output (`FormValues<E, Op, X>`; the extensions' values
 * under their keys).
 *
 * When formId is provided:
 * - Tracks form status (uploading/validating/submitting)
 * - Orchestrates file uploads before validation
 * - Provides cleanup function for unmount
 *
 * On a valid submit the page leaves for `successPath` (default: the previous
 * breadcrumb) before the server answers, and returns on rejection. Pass
 * `successPath: null` to stay.
 *
 * `handleSubmit()` without `onValid` uses the default writer: the record
 * (update, or add on create) with the fields the form writes, plus the child
 * rows joined to this form (`useChildRows` / a nested `EntityList`), in one
 * `bulkAcross`. With `onValid`, write the joined rows from `form.pendingWrites()`
 * (the submit fails explicitly when joined rows have edits and it was not read).
 *
 * @template E - Entity type from defineEntity()
 * @template Op - Form operation (`options.operation`; both when not given)
 * @template X - 1:1 extensions (`options.extend`), none by default
 * @param entity - Entity definition from defineEntity()
 * @param options - Form configuration options
 * @returns Form instance with React Hook Form API plus entity-aware extensions
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * const viewerRole = useAuth('userRole');
 * const form = useEntityForm(productEntity, {
 *   formId: 'product-create',
 *   operation: 'create',
 *   viewerRole,
 * });
 * // In the custom layout, for each editable field from form.fields:
 * // <FormFieldRenderer name={field.name} config={field.config}
 * //   control={form.control} t={form.t} />
 * ```
 */
export declare function useEntityForm<E extends AnyEntity, Op extends FieldOperation = FieldOperation, const X extends EntityExtensions = Record<never, never>>(entity: E, options?: UseEntityFormOptions<E, Op, X>): EntityFormReturn<E, Op, X>;

isFieldEditable:
/**
 * Determines if a field is edited as an input by the current viewer, from the
 * entity descriptor (`describeEntity(entity).fields[name].editableFor`): the same
 * rule as forms, grids and URL prefills.
 *
 * - Only the `user` write class is editable: `editable: 'generated'`, `'computed'`,
 *   `false`, hidden fields and backend names (`id`, `createdAt`, ...) never are
 * - `editable` unset / `true`: editable, except technical fields (read-only)
 * - `'create-only'`: editable on create only
 * - a role: `hasRoleAccess(viewerRole, role)` (guest < user < admin < super)
 *
 * NOTE: Visibility is handled by backend - this function only handles editability (UI concern).
 *
 * @param entity - Entity from `defineEntity()`
 * @param fieldName - Field name (key in `entity.fields`)
 * @param viewerRole - Current viewer's role
 * @param operation - Form operation type
 * @returns Whether the field should be rendered as an input (true) or read-only (false)
 * @throws When `entity` has no field `fieldName`
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * // fields: { title: {}, status: { editable: 'admin' }, sku: { editable: 'create-only' } }
 * isFieldEditable(productEntity, 'title', 'user', 'edit');  // true
 * isFieldEditable(productEntity, 'status', 'user', 'edit'); // false (user < admin)
 * isFieldEditable(productEntity, 'sku', 'admin', 'edit');   // false (create only)
 * isFieldEditable(productEntity, 'createdAt', 'super', 'edit'); // false (backend-generated)
 * ```
 *
 * @see `Editable` (`@donotdev/core`) for editable configuration options
 *
 * @version 0.2.0
 * @since 0.0.1
 * @author AMBROISE PARK Consulting
 */
export declare function isFieldEditable(entity: AnyEntity, fieldName: string, viewerRole: string, operation: FieldOperation): boolean;
getFieldsForOperation:
/**
 * Filters entity fields based on operation type and viewer role, from the entity
 * descriptor (`describeEntity`: write class, `editableFor`, visibility).
 *
 * Pure function, no React dependencies. Use for building custom form layouts.
 *
 * Per write class (design 3.4):
 * - `never` (hidden, `editable: 'generated'`, backend names): not shown, except
 *   technical fields on edit, shown read-only (`id`, `createdAt`, ...)
 * - `program` (`editable: false`): shown read-only
 * - `derived` (`editable: 'computed'`): shown read-only, written by the form
 * - `user`: an input when `editableFor(viewerRole, operation)`, else read-only
 *
 * **Create operation:** excludes `visibility: 'technical'` fields.
 * **Edit operation:** if `availableFields` is provided, only returns those fields.
 * Fields the viewer cannot see (`visibility` above the role, `hidden`) are left out.
 *
 * @param entity - Entity definition from defineEntity(), or a field map
 * @param options - Filtering options
 * @returns Array of renderable fields with computed editability
 * @throws When a field has a custom type and no value shape (`describeEntity`)
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * import { getFieldsForOperation } from '@donotdev/crud/forms';
 * import { productEntity } from './entities/product';
 *
 * const editFields = getFieldsForOperation(productEntity, {
 *   operation: 'edit',
 *   viewerRole: 'admin',
 * });
 *
 * // Inputs for written editable fields; read-only display for the others
 * // (`written`: from form state, else from form.record)
 * editFields.map(({ name, config, editable }) => (
 *   editable
 *     ? <Input key={name} {...config} />
 *     : <ReadOnlyDisplay key={name} {...config} />
 * ));
 * ```
 *
 * @see {@link AnyEntity} for entity definition structure
 * @see {@link RenderableField} for return type
 *
 * @version 0.2.0
 * @since 0.0.1
 * @author AMBROISE PARK Consulting
 */
export declare function getFieldsForOperation(entity: EntityFieldsInput, options: GetFieldsForOperationOptions): RenderableField[];

 *   type: 'select'
 * }, t);
 * // Returns: translated "status" from "common" namespace

 * Supports namespace:key syntax (e.g., "crud:status.draft")

UseEntityFormOptions:
/**
 * Options for useEntityForm hook.
 *
 * @template E - Entity type from defineEntity()
 * @template Op - Form operation (`operation`), both when not given
 * @template X - 1:1 extensions (`extend`), none by default
 *
 * @version 0.2.0
 * @since 0.0.1
 * @author AMBROISE PARK Consulting
 */
export interface UseEntityFormOptions<E extends AnyEntity, Op extends FieldOperation = FieldOperation, X extends EntityExtensions = Record<never, never>> {
    /**
     * Form ID for tracking form/upload state.
     * Required for deferred file uploads and form status tracking.
     * Also scopes the auto-saved draft: give each form on the same record its own
     * stable formId (e.g. 'product-prices') so their drafts never overwrite each other.
     */
    formId?: string;
    /**
     * Form operation type.
     * - 'create': Excludes technical fields, all other fields editable
     * - 'edit': Shows all fields from defaultValues, technical fields read-only
     * @default 'create' (or 'edit' if defaultValues provided)
     */
    operation?: Op;
    /**
     * Initial form values ({@link EntityFormDefaultValues}).
     * - edit: the stored row as read (already visibility-filtered), accepted as-is.
     *   It becomes `form.record`; form state holds only the fields the form writes.
     * - create: create defaults (e.g. `status: 'draft'`, a parent reference).
     * Fields the form does not write (generated, technical, `editable: false`,
     * role-denied) never enter form state, the local draft or the payload.
     */
    defaultValues?: EntityFormDefaultValues<E, Op>;
    /**
     * Viewer role for editability checks.
     * Determines which fields render as inputs vs read-only.
     * If not provided, defaults to 'guest' (most restrictive)
     * @default 'guest'
     */
    viewerRole?: string;
    /**
     * When fields validate (React Hook Form `mode`). Default `'onTouched'`: a field shows
     * its first error when the user leaves it, then re-validates on every change, so the
     * fix clears the error while typing ("reward early, punish late"). A submit validates
     * every field. `'onBlur'`: on leaving only; `'onChange'`: every keystroke from the start.
     * @default 'onTouched'
     */
    mode?: 'onBlur' | 'onChange' | 'onSubmit' | 'onTouched' | 'all';
    /**
     * Optional override for labels, hints, options and nested field-array fields.
     * Omit for normal usage: useEntityForm automatically uses
     * `useTranslation([entity.namespace, 'crud'])` with language/SSR support.
     * Supply your own translator only to bypass that namespace resolution; it
     * replaces the default translator completely. Pass returned `form.t` to the
     * field renderers in either case.
     */
    t?: (key: string, options?: Record<string, unknown>) => string;
    /**
     * Whether the form data is still loading (e.g. async fetch in edit mode).
     * When true, form initialization and draft restoration are deferred until false.
     * Transitions from true → false reset the draft guard so draft loads against the correct data.
     * @default false
     */
    loading?: boolean;
    /**
     * Where the page goes once a submit passes validation and uploads.
     * The form leaves right away, before the server answers (optimistic); if the
     * write rejects, it returns to the page it left and the saved draft restores
     * every edit.
     * - omitted: the previous breadcrumb (nearest existing parent route, else `/`)
     * - a path: that path
     * - `null`: stay on the page (dialogs, wizards, settings, create flows that
     *   open the new record, pages holding other unsaved state, and every form of
     *   a nested submit: leaving would unmount the inner form and cancel its save)
     *
     * Needs the router access `@donotdev/ui` provides; without it the form stays.
     */
    successPath?: string | null;
    /**
     * The form's own toasts: "fields to correct" when a submit fails validation,
     * and "draft restored" (default `true`). `false`: neither; the field messages,
     * the scroll to the first one and the draft restoring itself remain (a form in
     * a sheet or dialog). Success toasts have their own opt-outs:
     * `showSuccessToast` per mutation, `setHideSuccessToasts` on the CRUD store.
     * @default true
     */
    toasts?: boolean;
    /**
     * 1:1 extensions edited with the record (a record split across two tables,
     * e.g. `{ offer: { entity: productOfferEntity, field: 'productId' } }`): their
     * fields join `form.fields` prefixed `key.` (`offer.priceExclVat`; values under
     * `values.offer`), with conditions, validation, draft and uploads. In edit mode
     * the extension row is read (the form waits for it); the default writer and
     * `pendingWrites()` update it, or insert it when missing (after the record on
     * create). A viewer without read access to an extension entity gets none of it.
     * Keep the same keys while mounted.
     * @since 0.2.5
     */
    extend?: X;
}
EntityFormHandleSubmit:
/**
 * React Hook Form's `handleSubmit` (resolves `onValid`'s result, `undefined` when
 * the submit did not reach it) plus per-submit {@link EntityFormSubmitOptions}.
 *
 * `onValid` is optional: without it the default writer saves the record (update,
 * or add on create) with the fields the entity allows, plus the child rows joined
 * to the form, in one `bulkAcross`, and resolves its {@link BulkAcrossResult}.
 * With it, the app writes; joined rows' writes come from `form.pendingWrites()`.
 *
 * @template T - What `onValid` receives (the resolver's output)

 * - MAX only → include null/undefined
 * - MIN + MAX → exclude null/undefined

/**
 * React hook for CRUD Actions & Single Documents

 * Use this hook for:
 * - Checking feature status: `const status = useCrud('status');`
 * - Adding, Updating, Deleting items
 * - Fetching a single document
 *
 * **IMPORTANT: Always destructure the return value.**
 * The returned object is a new reference every render (same pattern as
 * TanStack Query). Individual methods (`get`, `query`, `add`, `update`,
 * `delete`) are `useCallback`-stable and safe as useEffect dependencies.

 * useEffect(() => { query({ limit: 50 }).then(setRows); }, [query]);
 *
 * // WRONG — infinite loop (new object every render)
 * const crud = useCrud<Car>(carEntity);
 * useEffect(() => { crud.query(...); }, [crud]); // loop!
 * ```

 * @param options - Configuration options
 * @returns CRUD Actions API (destructure before using in deps)
 */
